clippings.speaker: Clint Eastwood
clippings.quote: I'm sure he influenced me a lot. His boldness, subjectwise, and visually he was terrific.
clippings.title: EASTWOOD REMEMBERS `FISTFUL OF DOLLARS' DIRECTOR
clippings.context: At a Sundance (Park City) press conference in January 1990, a few months after Leone's death, Eastwood was asked about Leone's influence on his own directing.

clippings.speaker: Clint Eastwood
clippings.quote: It was very easy to handle that. I just did my own thing
clippings.title: EASTWOOD REMEMBERS `FISTFUL OF DOLLARS' DIRECTOR
clippings.context: At the same January 1990 Park City press conference, Eastwood described working with Leone despite the language gap.

clippings.speaker: Clint Eastwood
clippings.quote: He knew 'Goodbye' and I knew 'Arividerce', and that was about it
clippings.title: How was Clint Eastwood cast as the 'Man with No Name'?
clippings.context: Eastwood recalled the language barrier with Leone on Inside the Actors Studio in 2003, as quoted by Far Out Magazine in 2024.

clippings.speaker: Sergio Leone
clippings.quote: what I saw, simply, was a block of marble.
clippings.title: Sergio Leone Had An Interesting Take When Comparing Clint Eastwood And Robert De Niro
clippings.context: Leone, interviewed by American Film in 1984, recalled what he saw in Eastwood when he cast him in a 1964 Western TV-series role.

clippings.speaker: Sergio Leone
clippings.film: Once Upon a Time in America
clippings.title: Sergio Leone Had An Interesting Take When Comparing Clint Eastwood And Robert De Niro
clippings.context: Leone, in the 1984 American Film interview, contrasted Robert De Niro with Eastwood while discussing acting on Once Upon a Time in America.

notes: Leone-side quotes are all secondhand via SlashFilm; the Eastwood 1990 quotes come from a Deseret News piece. Fetch tooling returned summaries with a 125-character cap, so wording was checked only against the quoted text it returned, and the 1977 BBC and 1980 Gentry interview lines were skipped as fragments or unverifiable.
